Create one independent, randomized, complex photographic test scene for the arm-assigned vibraphone meaning, use the attachment only for bounded visible adult appearance cues, render the image, and judge whether the instrument semantics are actually visible in the pixels.

A photorealistic editorial photograph on an empty planetarium's circular stage during overnight projector calibration. An original adult vibraphonist performs on an unmistakable motor-equipped pedal vibraphone built around two rows of silvery metal bars. At the first motor-on downbeat, her two yarn-wrapped mallets make real playing contact with separate metal bars while her right foot visibly depresses the full-width damper pedal. Beneath the bar deck, complete ranks of vertical resonator tubes reveal circular motor-driven fan disks turning inside several tube mouths. This combined metal-bar deck, resonator bank, motor fans, and damping pedal establishes the instrument as a vibraphone, distinct from a xylophone's wooden-bar construction. Use Image 1 only for the original adult performer's visible facial appearance, long dark wavy hairstyle, restrained warm eye makeup, natural rose lips, and luminous skin-surface finish. A narrow amber follow spot intersects cool moving constellation projections and dim red aisle lights. A low 35 mm three-quarter view from the audience aisle keeps her face in the upper third, sends the bars diagonally through the frame, and preserves an unobstructed sightline under the instrument to the fans, resonators, pedal, and pressing foot.
